description_full: Grupo Supervielle S.A., a financial services holding company, provides various banking products and services in Argentina. The company operates through Personal & Business Banking, Corporate Banking, Bank Treasury, Insurance, and Asset Management and Other Services segments. It offers savings and checking accounts, and time deposits; personal, mortgage, unsecured, and car loans; overdrafts; loans with special facilities for project and working capital financing; and leasing, bank guarantees for tenants, salary advances, domestic and international factoring, international guarantees and letters of credit, payroll payment plans, and credit and debit cards, as well as financial services and investments, such as mutual funds, guarantees, and benefit payments for senior citizens. The company also provides foreign trade and cash management; advisory services; treasury services; insurance products comprising life, home, personal accidents, technology, ATMs, protected bag and content, and integral insurance product for entrepreneurs and SME customers and other insurance policies; and asset management and other services, as well as operates as a digital online broker. It operates through a network of branches, ATMs, and self-service terminals. The company was formerly known as Inversiones y Participaciones S.A. and changed its name to Grupo Supervielle S.A. in November 2008. Grupo Supervielle S.A. was founded in 1887 and is based in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

financial_summary: Grupo Supervielle S.A. is a small-cap financial services business with a $532M market cap on $942M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +17% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 37% against a 10% cost of capital — a 27-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.
Accruals are elevated at -10.4% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 7.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 22% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
